decisions.reason: Requiring comprehension by unfamiliar viewers strengthens the completed clip's standalone teaching behavior but does not change the existing source-material or moment-selection rules.
The unfamiliar-viewer comprehension requirement does not alter the independent requirement for an effective hook.
The comprehension requirement does not add, remove, or change any target publication channel.
Background-music presence and volume remain valid unchanged; their appearance in the same message is independent of the comprehension modification.
The new comprehension standard applies to the first live clips and does not retroactively modify the completed initial trial assignment.
The batch still requires five first-production clips; unfamiliar-viewer comprehension is an independent content standard rather than a change to the batch count or deliverable.
The requirement that unfamiliar viewers understand each clip does not change the existing clean-editing or effects policies.
Caption color, font, and effects rules remain unchanged by the standalone-comprehension requirement.
The requalification assignment had already been completed and accepted, and the new first-live-clip comprehension standard does not alter its historical task state.
The client reiterates prepublication review, but the comprehension modification does not change approval authority, counting, rejection, or publication-gate mechanics.
Natural B-roll placement is an independent standard introduced in the same message and is not changed by the unfamiliar-viewer comprehension decision.
The 45-to-60-second duration state remains unchanged; comprehension by unfamiliar viewers imposes a separate content criterion.
